boundary_evidence: The class's complete member set in one contiguous run: LookAt_ at 0x02055a64 through PerspectiveW_ ending at 0x02055dec -- config/arm9/symbols.txt records exactly two _ZN3G3i symbols, both here.

func_02055998 below and GXS::EndLoadOBJExtPltt (0x02055dec) above are neighbours in the gx block, not members: the former is an unenrolled free function, the latter belongs to GXS's OBJ-extended-palette loader set.
No lifecycle or RTTI: G3i has no instance state and no virtuals (include/G3i.h documents the all-static shape), so nothing but the two functions emits.

compiler_only_output.reason: LookAt_ declares three stack Vector3s; types.h gives Vector3 a non-trivial (empty) destructor, so the front end emits D1 in this TU but elides every call site. The cartridge body (four bytes, bx lr) has a configured home at 0x020072c0 owned by src/named/arm9/_ZN7Vector3D1Ev.cpp, so this emitted copy deadstrips as a duplicate.

notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/G2x entry, which took the same route.

G3i is the geometry engine's immediate-mode matrix writer set. LookAt_ composes the camera basis (right/up2/forward via CrossVec3/NormalizeVec3/DotVec3) and streams it to the position-matrix port 0x400045c under matrix mode 2; PerspectiveW_ runs the 64-bit division unit at 0x4000290 for cot/depth terms and streams the projection rows to 0x4000458 under mode 0. Both optionally mirror the matrix into a caller Matrix4x3.

PerspectiveW_ stays a literal-mangled `extern "C"` definition under `#pragma cplusplus off`: its six by-value Fix12<int> parameters are the by-value-class ABI wall (the include/OAM.h note), and its ROM body is the C front end's output. include/G3i.h deliberately does not declare it; callers keep `extern "C"` declarations of the literal symbol.
The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order under default deferred codegen; the emitted object carries the two functions ascending 0x02055a64..0x02055dec.
